matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(gateway): keep CLI session model identities consistent (#139884)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(gateway): keep CLI session model identities consistent (#139884)

Related: #136257

## What Problem This Solves

Sessions selected through a CLI backend can show different model providers in the session list, details, and patch response. Details can borrow the unrelated agent default, and searching by the actual provider can miss the session. Standalone backends can also lose their own identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway uses the existing backend's declared model provider for display identity. Lists, defaults, details, search, and patch responses share that projection. Catalog and runtime policy keep the original selected route, including existing CLI-specific context metadata.

Removed provider guessing from agent defaults/configured model names, the lightweight-row bypass, and the obsolete agent-specific display cache key. This is an existing read-surface repair; it adds no protocol fields, authentication mutation, configuration option, or storage change.

## User Impact

- Model provider and model identity agree across session reads.
- Provider/model search includes sessions selected through their CLI backend.
- Qualified identities and standalone backend names remain intact.
- Stored selections, runtime policy, and selected-route catalog metadata keep their owners.

## Evidence

The actual built Gateway was tested with the bundled Claude CLI descriptor and two isolated fixture backends. All requests used synthetic state without inference or operator credentials.

| Existing API scenario | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List and describe one mapped CLI selection | CLI name in list; unrelated default provider in details | Declared provider in both |
| Standalone CLI details | Unrelated default provider | Standalone backend identity |
| Qualified CLI selection | Different list/detail identities | Same qualified identity |
| CLI agent default | Runtime alias shown as provider | Declared model provider |
| Provider/model search | Mapped CLI selection omitted | Selection included |
| Label-only session patch | Unrelated provider in response | Declared provider; selection unchanged |

Baseline `2a488546aabe1921259e7d3a4f18be8f3741d77d`; candidate `f29a4e100a3040db6904b8cc0b27f07d2fac328c`. Three new regression cases fail on the original production code; the direct-provider control passes. All 246 affected identity/session tests pass after the repair. Existing context-window assertions remain unchanged. ACP ownership and resolver-cache checks also pass. Focused syntax lint, pinned formatting, assertion-safety and max-lines checks pass. Type checks run in CI.

A fresh source-blind, API-only validator exercised 117 complete request/response pairs and 20 real session events. Identity, search, label-patch, standalone/qualified controls, and changed-default/restoration checks pass. It found no observable model-identity failure. Retained selection fields remain unchanged. Inference was intentionally excluded; APIs/logs cannot prove absence of unlogged work. Build isolation and historical baseline provenance are supplied by the repair owner, not claimed as independently discoverable through the API. An earlier validator inspected the synthetic database schema; its evidence is retained only as supplemental proof, not as the source-blind gate.

Production: **+41/-58, net -17**. Tests: **+102**. Total: **+85**. No generated, lockfile, or docs changes. The added regression matrix checks full/lightweight rows, patch responses, defaults, search, and retained runtime policy at existing boundaries; it adds no test-only production seam. No existing coverage was removed.

AI-assisted.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(channels): unify progress cards and native rendering (#139206)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(channels): unify progress cards and native rendering (#139206)

## What Problem This Solves

Progress-card updates could print raw renderer HTML as tool text, disappear from compact previews, or lose the valid plan when the model started its next message. A clear could then remove unrelated activity. Native notifications and the request transcript also had competing summary-emission paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared compositor owns one complete plan snapshot and its update/clear lifecycle across preview modes. Model-message boundaries preserve that plan and current activity; actual answer transitions reset transient activity, and a new user turn resets the full state.

- File-edit totals use one shared formatter, reused by Slack, generic previews, and Telegram. Clearing a plan retains real edit totals without leaving stale plan text.
- Streams without deletion support, including Teams, retain the shipped neutral-label replacement when clearing an existing preview. Initial empty clears remain silent.
- Channel adapters consume the shared snapshot instead of maintaining separate preview plans.
- Telegram renders native checkbox lists with the existing `channels.telegram.richMessages: true` setting, and readable HTML otherwise.
- Complete status updates can start a preview without disabling ordinary token-stream debouncing.
- Failed or blocked writes retain the valid plan and use safe tool labels.
- Dynamic tool output is consolidated under the request/transcript owner instead of competing native-notification formatting paths.
- The shipped standalone plan-line helper keeps its prior representation. Shared selection, compaction, and attention helpers support native channel rendering.

## User Impact

A checklist remains visible across tool calls. Clearing it removes the plan while retaining unrelated command or failure activity. Later updates can recreate the card, and final delivery still completes normally.

The durable web card remains the source of the stored plan and note. Channel summaries use structured steps and a completion count, or `Progress updated` for a note-only card, rather than interpreting renderer HTML.

## Evidence

Baseline: `41fba39c40aa2840d7a3a8bb24eeac525c871ac9`. The original markup leak and blocked-row behavior were reproduced through Telegram's Test Server. The regression suite includes real assistant-message boundaries and actual draft transports behind mocked channel APIs.

The test sequence is: empty clear → checklist plus HTML → note-only HTML → clear → new plan → invalid status → harmless command → clear preserving activity → completed plan → final reply.

Prepared head: `092c97af3276c6e2c5252b37ac9ecffffe64c7ef`.

- Telegram Test Server: rich and HTML progress, partial, and block previews; native checkbox states, short updates, clear/recreate, retained activity, blocked calls, final replies, and cleanup verified.
- Retained progress runs on `d6462474` prove exactly one command row for one command call. A separate queued-followup run proves both replies, a queued plan, and one queued command row with normal verbosity.
- Default-label clear/recreate was reproduced before repair and verified through native rich progress and plain partial Telegram previews at `cfc97d17`. Those runs use no file-edit tool, so the later diff-stat-only addition does not change their inputs. The owner suite also covers default, disabled, and custom labels in all three modes.
- Partial/block captures remain bound to `f2a5c514fd327b0c96c4e28314ef5268002ccec6`. The later change removes a flag that was already false in those primary-turn modes, plus changes queued-turn gating. Focused tests cover the final source; affected progress/queued live runs were repeated.
- Focused producer, compositor, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, and Mattermost tests pass. Tests ran in an isolated Linux container; formatting and scoped lint pass.
- SDK surface check passes. The metadata reader needed an explicit 6 GiB heap after the container default ran out of memory; no source/test failure was hidden.
- Native Telegram proof at `5763533` also covers quiet progress with labels hidden: plan → actual two-line write → clear leaves the edit summary → completed plan → final reply and cleanup.
- The final runtime adjustment only reaches adapters without a deletion callback; Telegram always provides one. Retained live proof remains applicable. Teams default/custom-label clear, recreation, and final delivery pass through its real SDK and an HTTP loopback provider; there is no live Teams-service claim. Hidden-label Teams previews retain their existing interim limitation, now stated in the streaming docs.
- Actual Codex app-server `0.153.4`, real inference, real tools, and Telegram Test Server: main `b3bdf3e1` displays literal card HTML as fixed-width text; this head displays the two correct native checkbox states. Both calls persist successfully and finish normally.
- Actual native read comparison: one execution, one summary, one result, and one final on both main and candidate. No read-output duplicate was reproduced; that Codex change is ownership consolidation, not a claimed duplicate-message repair.
- Independent source-blind acceptance and diff-scoped cleanup pass. Landing requires exact-head CI and the local correctness review.
- Production: **+568/-581, net -13**. Tests/support: **+1934/-485**. Docs: **+18/-4**. Tooling: **+11/-5**. Generated metadata: **+1/-1**.

Relevant commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.progress-updates.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.progress-card.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts
node --max-old-space-size=6144 --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts --check
```

The earlier CI cleanup derives Matrix's handle type from its factory, removes unused formatting helpers, consolidates a test root, and synchronizes generated tool metadata. Those cleanup edits did not change active Telegram behavior. A subsequent shared-owner repair makes retraction check remaining activity, headline, plan, and diff statistics before rendering, so a decorative label cannot keep an empty card alive.

The shared projection, native-rendering, and edit-summary helpers are additive SDK exports. The existing deprecated wildcard barrel forwards them; its inventory is updated without introducing another compatibility path. Live network proof is Telegram-specific; sibling channels are covered by their real controller/transport code against mocked APIs.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

Both plugins now use the existing catalog outcome owner. Google reuses strict acquisition at registration, preserves the released helper's advisory default through the existing selector, and keeps Vertex in its static owner. Copilot resolves credentials once, preserves the selected profile and HTTP status through acquisition, and removes its redundant text-catalog producer. Request-time fallback and existing credential/header validation remain intact.

## User Impact

Failed refreshes report catalog rejection or unavailability and retain compatible last-successful inventory. Successful empty responses are authoritative. Missing credentials and disabled discovery make no live attempt.

## Evidence

- Built baseline `2d361a8cdbaf`: controlled Google and Copilot HTTP503 responses produced no failure outcomes; successful empty Google inventory still displayed ten bundled rows.
- Fourteen regression cases fail against original baseline production; all 156 focused cases pass across catalog, profile selection, request preparation, headers, response parsing and sibling behavior.
- Independent source review: no findings through P2. Formatting, syntax lint, assertion safety, maximum-line and coercion checks pass. The assertion baseline only removes the two eliminated Google casts.
- Published `openclaw@2026.9.2` artifact and tag inspected: Google's exported helper keeps advisory fallback by default. Built default/strict calls confirm fallback versus truthful failure/empty behavior over controlled HTTPS.
- Production: -38 lines; tests/support: +31; docs: +1; check metadata: -1; total: -7.

Independent built-product acceptance passes the scoped contract: truthful 401/403/503, socket and malformed-response outcomes; retained inventory and recovery; authoritative empty; zero-auth/disabled non-attempts; static Vertex; direct/profile provenance; valid provider-key references; and account switching with context limits `128000 → 96000 → 128000` and actual request output limits `4096 → 2048 → 4096`. Catalog refresh performs one Google request and at most one Copilot account request plus one model request. Four synthetic completions verify request-time behavior. The passing reports retain the earlier blocked/failed fixture observations and their resolutions.

Candidate runtime inputs match `e63dcc37b1d9`; the retained build stamp correctly identifies its parent plus the frozen patch, not a later clean build. Vendor checks use unauthenticated endpoints and controlled HTTPS responses with synthetic credentials, not authenticated vendor inference.

Known baseline limitation: an integration-header SecretRef passes CLI validation but fails catalog refresh. The exact pinned baseline reproduces the same direct-key → header-reference sequence. Shared config materialization is outside this producer change; the failure remains a named follow-up, not a claimed fix. matched_commits.full_message:
fix(docker): stage bundled plugin runtime dependencies under the packaged plugin root (#139117)

The official 2026.9.1 image cannot load its bundled externally distributed
plugins (codex, diagnostics-otel): doctor and plugins inspect report every
declared dependency as missing. Since the workspace moved to pnpm's isolated
linker (#135728) those packages live only in /app/node_modules/.pnpm and are
linked from /app/extensions/<id>/node_modules, neither of which is an ancestor
of the packaged root /app/dist/extensions/<id> that the dependency lookup
(src/plugins/status-dependencies-core.ts) and the managed Codex launcher
resolution (extensions/codex/src/app-server/managed-binary.ts) start from.
2026.8.2 worked only because the hoisted linker placed them in
/app/node_modules. Docker-selected plugins are built as unified outputs, so
the source-checkout dependency links added in #135903 never applied to them.

Move linkSourcePluginDependencies into a plain-Node module and have the
Docker assembly stage link each retained root-package-excluded plugin's
production install under dist/extensions/<id>/node_modules after package
lifecycle cleanup, failing the image build when a declared dependency still
does not resolve from the packaged root.

Fixes #138777. Reported by 8bitsforge.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: perf(sessions): stop decoding the session row four times per SQLite entry patch (#136361)
matched_commits.full_message:
perf(sessions): stop decoding the session row four times per SQLite entry patch (#136361)

patchSqliteSessionEntrySnapshot read and JSON-decoded the session row at
preparation, again inside the write transaction to revalidate (then
JSON.stringify-compared both copies), a third time inside writeSessionEntry for
the canonical previous entry, and a fourth time after the write for the identity
diff, running the participants projection query on every decode. A streamed
reply turn issues about eleven such patches, so with a prod-shaped ~17 KB
entry_json the session store took 29% of a saturated gateway main thread on
2026.8.2 against 3.6% for the JSON store on 2026.7.1-2.

Snapshot rows now carry the raw persisted row they were decoded from. At commit,
readUnchangedLifecycleTargetSnapshot re-reads the raw rows for exactly the keys
the snapshot reader consults and reuses the prepared snapshot when every column
is identical; any difference falls back to the original full re-decode and deep
compare, so conflict detection is unchanged. writeSessionEntry accepts the
canonical previous entry the commit already holds, and the post-commit identity
map is built from the persisted entry, which is all the diff reads.

No transaction boundary, writer ownership, publication fencing, schema or
persisted representation changes. The revalidation reader lives in its own
module because the entry store is at its max-lines limit.

AI-assisted (Claude Code); measured, tested and reviewed by the author.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(gateway): deliver loopback ask_user prompts to the originating channel (#138831)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(gateway): deliver loopback ask_user prompts to the originating channel (#138831)

Closes #138540

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting a Claude CLI turn from Telegram would receive no interactive question when the turn called `ask_user` through loopback MCP. The question existed in Gateway state, but the originating chat received only a working indicator and eventually a timeout explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway tool construction now uses the existing portable question publisher for the originating channel, account, and conversation. One shared question lifetime ends unfinished publication before cancellation or post-answer metadata work.

The durable delivery owner retires its exact, still-unsent claim when cancellation arrives during adapter preparation. Preparation remains attached so its eventual resource token and queued media receive normal cleanup. Dispatched, sent, ambiguous, expired-lease, and replacement-owned deliveries retain their existing settlement rules.

## User Impact

Users receive the question and its choices in Telegram, answer with native controls or the existing text-answer path, and continue the original tool call. Ended questions cannot later publish or replay a proven-unsent prompt. Credential requests retain the existing Control UI link, native-only, and missing-public-link guidance.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `00338b642990bb5c65fa514f231606031dcf5bad`. Live product proof was run on `8034bbbe5bfca7274fcd9b8f6956cac33e8d6a67` and is retained under the unchanged-owner assessment below.

- **Real baseline:** current main `d0137988844d201423fbe1918e8c5acef8ddfa8e`, Telegram Test Server user → Gateway → Claude CLI → `mcp__openclaw__ask_user`. Gateway listed the destination question as pending. Telegram received no question during the tool wait; the CLI eventually returned a timeout. The initial raw observer needed device identity; the canonical Gateway client captured the pending record during the same run. The observation-command failure and all earlier setup results are retained separately from product evidence.
- **Real candidate:** the same entry path delivered one question with Staging and Production buttons. The user clicked Production. The same question changed to “Answered: Production,” and Claude confirmed Production after the tool returned the answer. Recording completed successfully, including the Gateway observer and native callback action.
- **Supported-entrypoint cancellation / SDK hardening:** the same installed-plugin fixture ran through native Gateway `agent` → real Claude CLI → loopback `ask_user`. It held the public channel adapter's preparation callback, cancelled the actual question through `question.resolve`, invoked published SDK recovery while held and after release, then submitted a fresh authorized request in the same session. Intake `45e8624bbe03` replayed the cancelled question after preparation returned. Candidate `8034bbbe5bfc` produced no stale send or recovery candidate, released the late resource once, and delivered “Proceeding with destination Alpha.” The native transcript confirms cancellation returned to the original MCP tool-use ID. This uses published package exports and an installed synthetic transport, with no internal source imports; physical Telegram behavior remains covered by the two retained real Telegram runs.
- **Regression proof:** the original contributor head failed both a held-metadata publication test and a held-adapter queue-retirement test. The repaired head passes both. Recovery while preparation remains held makes no send; late preparation releases its token once. Restored media, replacement claims, sent/ambiguous outcomes, and lease failure retain coverage.
- **Pinned base refresh:** merged upstream `886aaa689076b7b7c2f7a4d8d0048e89f5855698`, which contains #139176's correction to the exact failing CI assertion. The question, cancellation, delivery queue, Telegram and Claude CLI owners remain byte-identical to the live-tested head; dependencies and build inputs are unchanged. Adjacent startup/session changes were inspected, and 192 focused tests passed on the refreshed source, including the corrected spawn case, loopback delivery, CLI parsing and session-cache behavior. No Telegram setup or unchanged acceptance was repeated; earlier failures and build identities remain preserved.
- **Focused checks:** 194 tests passed across question tools, native harness questions, outbound queues/leases, Gateway tool resolution, loopback MCP authority, and Telegram question handling. Formatting with pinned oxfmt 0.65.0 and syntax lint pass. Type-aware lint exceeded the isolated proof resource limit; hosted exact-head CI remains required before landing.
- **Independent acceptance:** all six prewritten contract clauses passed. The validator authored a different Amber/Cobalt decision, submitted it through a prepared Telegram lease, clicked Cobalt, and verified the exact tool result and matching confirmation. It also judged 20 lifetime/recovery cases from 640 raw observations; diagnostic transport and synthetic-secret limits are retained.

Commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/secrets-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/ask-user-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/ask-user-tool-normalization.test.ts src/agents/harness/gateway-question.test.ts src/agents/tools/question-prompt-send.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/deliver-queue.cancellation-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver-queue.lease-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts test/loopback-ask-user-telegram-channel.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.question-authority.test.ts test/telegram-question-gateway.test.ts
```

The lifetime observation interface uses production question/delivery/queue/recovery owners with an explicitly synthetic adapter. It includes the real question-manager expiry timer and actual harness answer/cancel paths. Some Gateway terminal inputs remain supplied by the fixture. It complements the real Telegram/Claude flow; it does not claim physical native-app clicks, real secret storage, or a second replacement ingress run.

Production delta: +293/-84 (+209). The added behavior is the missing loopback publisher and immediate claim-fenced cancellation with delayed resource cleanup; neither existed at those owner boundaries. The schema moved unchanged beside input normalization, and duplicate publication-abort and durable-outcome branches were removed. Test delta: +1060/-63, including moved normalization coverage.

The five retained ClawSweeper moves are addressed by canonical outbound abort checks, immediate credential publication closure, atomic unsent-custody retirement, preserved credential guidance, and owner/sibling regression proof.

Separate observed follow-up: Claude CLI ended a 120-second Gateway question call after approximately 60 seconds. Aligning that client deadline with question lifetime is outside this repair's timeout scope.

Original repair by @ericcaiwx-star; reported by @drsnett. Maintainer repair and validation are AI-assisted.

The original [CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33980427913) remains recorded. This refresh adopts the merged correction to that assertion and requires normal exact-head CI; no historical-causality claim or CI bypass is used.

Additional observed follow-up: startup logs a duplicate `/dashboard` command registration. The question workflow completed; the warning is not attributed to this change.

fix(cli): automations runs required --id while sibling commands took a positional id (#138438)

* fix(cli): automations runs required --id while sibling commands took a positional id

`openclaw automations runs` was the only automation subcommand that refused a
positional job id and demanded `--id <id>`; `show`, `run`, `edit`, `remove` and
`scratch` all take `<id>` directly. The reference docs even list the two forms on
adjacent lines. Running `automations runs <id>` failed with
`Missing required option "--id <id>"`.

`runs` now accepts `[id]` positionally like its siblings and keeps `--id <id>` as
an equivalent alias so existing scripts keep working. Supplying two different ids
is rejected before any gateway call, and a missing id gets a message that names
the positional form. Docs updated to the positional form with a note that `--id`
remains accepted.

* fix(plugins): log warn-level plugin diagnostics through the warn sink

`logGatewayPluginDiagnostics` routed every non-error diagnostic through
`log.info`. `PluginDiagnostic.level` is only `"warn" | "error"`, so that
`else` branch is not a fallback for some residual level — it is *every*
warn diagnostic the plugin registry records, printed one severity level
below where it was recorded.

The consequence is that a degraded plugin surface cannot be found by a
level-filtered read of the journal. A warn that fires on every startup
sits indistinguishable from routine plugin chatter, so the operator sees
nothing when a plugin is running with part of itself disabled.

This is a logging-correctness fix only: no diagnostic is added, removed,
or reworded, and the error path is untouched. The `Pick` widens from
`"error" | "info"` to `"error" | "warn"`; the caller already passes the
full `GatewayPluginBootstrapLog`, which has carried `warn` all along.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(agents): keep OAuth MCP tools available to CLI agents (#136331)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(agents): keep OAuth MCP tools available to CLI agents (#136331)

Closes #136238

## What Problem This Solves

CLI agents can lose every tool from an OAuth-authenticated MCP server during native policy discovery. The child CLI projection stores the token in an environment variable, but the in-process discovery runtime received the literal environment placeholder after `auth: "oauth"` was removed. The server rejected that placeholder, and native refresh could not run.

## Root cause

`prepareCliBundleMcpConfig` used one projected server config for two consumers with different credential contracts:

- The in-process MCP runtime needs the original OAuth definition so OpenClaw can refresh after HTTP 401.
- The spawned CLI needs the environment-backed bearer projection so credentials do not enter its generated configuration as OpenClaw-only OAuth fields.

## Fix

- Give native policy discovery the original OAuth-capable definitions, filtered to the servers that survived projection and setup.
- Reproject only final policy survivors after discovery so each child backend receives the current bearer.
- Keep unavailable OAuth servers absent from both native discovery and the child configuration.
- Route the mock-heavy regression through the isolated agents shard.
- Fix an existing CI assertion to measure pending queue depth instead of double-counting an in-flight item that is intentionally retained in queue storage.

## Evidence

- Current main `4adab7342dd8ad3ba4311f5e0f9ff725c02fc3c7`: `openclaw agent --local` through the real `claude-cli` runtime sent one generated bearer placeholder during native `initialize`. Refresh did not run and `tools/list` never occurred. Baseline build: Testbox run `33647227596`.
- Exact head `28661c137ee1c4ee62976ad15c7e8dca77e239c9`: the same shipped command and runtime observed stale bearer, HTTP 401, fresh native initialization, fresh child initialization, fresh child `tools/list`, and fresh child `tools/call`. The agent returned `MCP_OAUTH_OK`.
- Anti-cheat: the server recorded every request method and classified each observed Authorization header. No placeholder reached the head path.

## Additional checks

- Focused OAuth, transport, Claude, Gemini, Codex, and native-policy tests: 79 passed across four Vitest shards.
- Test routing: 614 passed.
- Startup-recovery CI reproduction: failed before with one in-flight item retained among two raw items; passed after using the queue-depth owner, with one pending item.
- Reusable command: `node scripts/e2e/cli-backend-oauth-mcp-live.mjs`.

Local TypeScript checks and builds were not run because this maintainer host forbids them. Exact-head CI owns those checks.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: perf(ui,gateway): faster chat deep-link cold load: compress WebSocket frames, gate transcript warming (#136862)
matched_commits.full_message:
perf(ui,gateway): faster chat deep-link cold load: compress WebSocket frames, gate transcript warming (#136862)

* perf(gateway): negotiate permessage-deflate for large WebSocket frames

The Gateway never offered permessage-deflate, so a 338-message session's
chat.startup crossed the socket as a 1.92 MB frame (263 KB gzip). Offer
the extension with no context takeover on either side (bounded memory
per connection) and a 4 KiB threshold so streaming deltas and acks stay
raw while transcript and roster payloads compress 5-8x.

The post-auth receiver handoff now raises the negotiated deflate
extension's own payload limit together with the receiver's: ws@8.21.3
constructs PerMessageDeflate with the pre-auth maxPayload and its
inflateOnData rejects larger inflated data with 1009, so raising only
the receiver would still close the socket on the first compressed
post-auth transcript. Worker connections share the same helper.

Peers that do not offer the extension (Tauri's tokio-tungstenite, ESP
nodes) are byte-for-byte unaffected; browsers, Node ws clients,
Foundation (iOS/macOS) and OkHttp (Android) negotiate it and were
live-tested. docs/gateway/protocol.md documents the negotiated
compression and that limits apply to the inflated size.

* perf(ui): gate recent-session warming on owner-reported transcript loading edges

The chat page warmed the five most recent sessions with parallel
chat.history requests 250 ms after connect, 12.7 MB on the same socket
while the presented transcript was still pending; in the live trace this
stretched avatars, fonts and provider icons to 7-9 s.

Warming now runs only while no presented pane is loading its transcript,
rechecks that fact before each queued candidate, and fetches one session
at a time in recency order. The fact is recorded where it happens: every
transcript load phase write goes through setChatHistoryLoad, which calls
the pane-wired transcriptLoadingChanged hook on each loading edge; the
pane dispatches openclaw-chat-transcript-loading-changed and the prefetch
controller resamples on that single event. Session-event reloads never
re-render the page, so no page update could carry the edge, and no render
is spent on it.

Regressions at three levels: the controller resamples on the pane's edge
without a host update, a real ChatPane state reports start and commit
edges from loadChatHistory with coalesced re-entries silent, and a
Playwright run against the real ChatPage/ChatPane holds a session.message
reload on the wire while the prefetcher's cooldown retry fires and checks
that warming resumes once the reload commits.

* fix(gateway,ui): fail worker payload handoff visibly and recheck warming readiness per request

Two readiness races from review. The worker admission path ignored a
false return from raiseGatewayReceiverPayloadLimit and still advertised
worker-hello-ok; a later compressed frame above the pre-auth cap would
then close the socket mid-stream instead of failing the handshake. The
worker is now rejected before hello with UNAVAILABLE "unsupported
Gateway WebSocket receiver", close 1011 gateway-unavailable, and the
control-log reason unsupported-websocket-receiver, matching the operator
path. The public worker ingress test negotiates permessage-deflate like
production and covers a frozen receiver limit and a frozen deflate limit.

The prefetcher checked presented-transcript readiness before its
IndexedDB snapshot read but not after it, so a pane that started loading
during that await still got a background chat.history on the socket.
One mayRequest predicate (snapshot current and transcripts ready) now
runs immediately before every request, including the cursor-reset
refetch and the page-continuation callback, and the cooldown stamp moved
to the request itself so a candidate that yields stays eligible for the
cycle after the transcript commits.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(agents): recover catalog worker after generation mismatch (#127712)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(agents): recover catalog worker after generation mismatch (#127712)

## What Problem This Solves

A transient prepared model catalog fingerprint mismatch can permanently wedge one worker. Every later catalog or authentication request on that owner then repeats the cached preparation failure.

The failure reaches Gateway catalog and authentication reads used before agent dispatch.

## Root cause

The worker caches one `preparedGeneration` promise for its lifetime. A fingerprint mismatch rejects that promise. The parent receives the failure as a normal worker result, so it keeps the same worker and reuses the same rejected promise.

## Fix

- Return a typed generation-mismatch result before any catalog or authentication facts leave the worker.
- Reject that result in the pool validator so the pool closes before queued work can dispatch.
- Drop only the mismatched pool and let the same lifecycle owner create a new worker on the next request.
- Keep crashes, timeouts, and superseded generations permanently closed.
- Isolate the real-worker regression from ambient Codex authentication.

A persistent mismatch still rejects one request per cold worker. This bounded fail-closed behavior is intentional: it preserves the owner generation and avoids publishing foreign facts while the separate environmental drift remains under diagnosis.

Production change: +90/-33 lines, net +57. The remaining growth defines the typed mismatch result and the mismatch-only pool replacement. The maintainer pass removed the second terminal-error cache and the test-only error export.

The separate owner-publication race from #127710 has already landed through #130856. This pull request stays focused on the catalog-worker wedge.

## Evidence

Current main baseline: `5778f39cc39737ce63a7cfd9e2c254e26fc52293`

Red:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.wedge.proof.test.ts
1 failed, 1 passed
recovery on the same owner failed with:
prepared model catalog worker reconstructed a different runtime generation
```

The control case created a fresh owner from the unchanged plan and passed. This proves the fixture was valid and the existing worker was wedged.

Green on `90900cfcdc5e2affa5217ed06bf5d3558da09d57`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.integration.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.mismatch.integration.test.ts src/infra/worker-task-pool.test.ts
3 files passed, 34 tests passed
```

The transient case uses the real catalog owner, `WorkerTaskPool`, and worker thread. It proves queued work does not run on the retired worker, then proves worker 2 serves catalog and authentication facts on the same owner.

Original diagnosis and repair by @kiranvk-2011.

## CI note

Exact-head CI passed all selected jobs except `checks-node-compact-small-6`. Its unchanged `agent-exec` service-relay timing test failed twice while waiting for a fake CLI process ID. Current main commit `c3a495d198fe16e5a698132983ee1d7f7117d91a` removes that test, and this pull request does not touch its file or wait helper, so the squash merge cannot restore the failure. The latest PR context and evidence run passed after the required headings were restored.

## Problem

Direct-dispatch harnesses registered `ask_user` and `secrets` questions but did not publish the prompt into the conversation that needed to answer it. Codex normal turns, Codex `/btw` side threads, and Copilot use direct tool dispatch.

The embedded tool-start lifecycle owns prompt publication only when it creates a reservation. Direct dispatch has no reservation, so the question tools waited for an answer to a prompt that was never shown.

The question tools publish through the documented `questionPrompt` callback only when no lifecycle reservation exists. Embedded runs keep their existing reservation and publish exactly once. matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(agents): keep cache-TTL pruning sticky and use Anthropic server-side clearing (#137021)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(agents): keep cache-TTL pruning sticky and use Anthropic server-side clearing (#137021)

* fix(agents): keep cache-TTL pruning sticky and use Anthropic server-side clearing

Cache-TTL pruning projected soft-trimmed and hard-cleared tool results only
on the request where the TTL had expired. The very next request (a tool-loop
continuation or the next turn) sent the unpruned history again, so the prompt
cache diverged at the first pruned result and a prune cost an extra cache
write instead of saving one. On Claude Fable 5.1 the flip is a prefix edit:
thinking created during the pruned request is bound to the pruned bytes and
is dropped one request later.

- Record each cache-TTL projection in the session's tool-result projection
  state and freeze it, so every later request replays the same bytes; the
  TTL clock now gates new pruning rounds only. Soft trims derive from the
  canonical source, not the oversized projection, so bytes are reproducible.
- Persist the pruned keys and modes in the existing `openclaw.cache-ttl`
  transcript marker (key-sized, no result text) and re-derive the projection
  from canonical history on the first request after a Gateway restart.
  Compaction and reset drop projections whose source is gone; canonical
  recovery rewrites invalidate stale sources.
- On direct Anthropic API-key requests with `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"`
  delegate pruning to Anthropic's server-side `clear_tool_uses_20250919`
  edit (trigger max(50k, 30% of the window), keep 3 tool uses, clear at
  least max(12.5k, 5% of the window), tool exclusions derived from the
  configured allow/deny lists, inputs kept) in both Anthropic request paths
  through the shared payload policy, ordered before optional server
  compaction, with the `context-management-2025-06-27` beta added only when
  the edit is present. Applied edits from the final `message_delta` log one
  info line with counts only. OAuth, proxies, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and
  other providers keep the sticky client-side pruning.
- Docs: session pruning, anthropic provider page, logging.

* fix(agents): keep clearing and client pruning under one owner

- Replay existing cache-TTL projections even when Anthropic server-side
  clearing owns new pruning rounds, so a projection made on another route or
  restored from the transcript marker never flips back to full tool output.
- Hand the clearing request to the transport from the same runner decision
  that suspends client pruning; the Anthropic plugin wrapper is back to
  opt-in server compaction only.
- Read marker entries through the shared cache-TTL accessor so projection
  restore and the TTL reader see the same store.
- Compaction-replay eligibility fixture uses the Anthropic host required by
  the unified direct-route predicate.

* fix(agents): replay restored cache-TTL projections at the projection owner

Restored marker keys are materialized in projectToolResultBranch, which every
replay path uses (per-request history transform, cache-TTL prune pass,
recovery planning). A session keeps sending its pruned bytes after pruning is
switched off or the Gateway restarts; the prune pass loses its mode-specific
materialization loop. Hard clears persist their placeholder text in the
marker so restarts re-derive identical bytes; soft trims stay key-only.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix: memories never promote when the daily pass records a claim first (#136965)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix: memories never promote when the daily pass records a claim first (#136965)

Closes #136963

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with dreaming enabled would see `Promoted 0 candidate(s)` on every deep-sleep run — indefinitely — even though their memories were being recalled regularly. `MEMORY.md` never received durable promotions, and `openclaw memory promote` reported no candidates at all, giving no indication of why.

The trigger is ordering: when the dreaming daily pass records a claim **before** that claim's first interactive recall. That is the normal case, because the daily pass runs on a schedule and seeds claims before anything queries them.

## Why This Change Was Made

A claim's signals were being split across two store keys. The daily pass writes `memory:claim:<hash>`; a later recall of the same text could not land on that key, so it opened a rival path-qualified entry. Since `signalCount` is read per entry, both keys stayed permanently under `minRecallCount`/`minUniqueQueries`, and no amount of genuine use could move either one.

The opposite order — recall first, then daily — was already reconciled by the `nonDailyEntry` lookup, whose comment states the intent: "Daily recurrence reinforces that candidate instead of creating a rival." This change makes that intent hold in both directions for recall and grounded staging by applying one mirrored daily-claim lookup to every non-daily signal.

It also extends the citation-preservation rule to both paths. A daily claim key omits the file path, so later signals keep the original source citation rather than adopting whichever file the search or backfill happened to hit.

Thresholds and scoring are untouched — this only stops equivalent signals from being split.

## User Impact

Workspaces whose claims are seeded by the daily pass before being recalled or grounded now accumulate signals on a single entry, so genuine use reaches the promotion gate as designed. No configuration change or threshold tuning is needed.

## Evidence

- Current `main` at `53066564532e4ce55eca937c406cab85eee850e6` reproduced the daily-first recall split: two rival entries and zero candidates at two signals and two unique queries.
- The untouched PR head reproduced the same daily-first grounded split: two rival entries and zero candidates at the same thresholds.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts` — 93 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/` — 1,331 passed, 3 skipped.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-record.ts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Real workspace promotion trace through the production recorder, ranker, and apply path: daily-first plus three recalls produced one entry with `dailyCount=1`, `recallCount=3`, `signalCount=4`, and four unique queries; ranking returned one candidate; apply wrote one promotion to `MEMORY.md` with the original `memory/2026-04-01.md:3-3` citation.
- Real grounded staging trace: daily-first plus two grounded observations produced one entry with `dailyCount=1`, `groundedCount=2`, three signals, and three unique queries; ranking and apply each returned one result with the original daily citation.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix: gateway restart hangs while followup drain retries a draining error (#136713)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix: gateway restart hangs while followup drain retries a draining error (#136713)

Closes #136684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators restarting a Gateway with a queued follow-up could wait several minutes for shutdown. The queued turn retried after restart admission rejected it, so the old Gateway stayed active until its shutdown deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up queue now follows the existing one-way restart signal. When restart drain commits, it retires process-local queue work and its old callback before the Gateway inspects active work. A reversible restart-signal fence still waits for settlement and retries after rollback.

Durable accepted-input recovery remains the restart owner. The old in-memory queue and execution authority do not cross restart, as documented in `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md`.

## User Impact

A Gateway with a queued follow-up can finish a supervised restart on the normal shutdown path instead of emitting a retry burst until forced termination. If restart signal admission rolls back, the queued follow-up resumes normally.

## Evidence

Current-main red at `3100ba535f1d003d67a6a7536deacf8666367b38`:

- Blacksmith child-Gateway run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33711422936
- One held model turn, one confirmed queued same-session follow-up, then `SIGTERM`.
- Queued case reached the real follow-up admission path and emitted `7` `followup queue drain failed` events.
- No-queue control emitted `0` drain failures.

Exact repaired tree at `2baff4f9ed3f84dc9493149dcc20fed441c9baea`:

- Blacksmith exact-tree run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33714572460
- The same child-Gateway scenario emitted no retry burst and exited in `3.465s`.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue.drain-restart.test.ts`: `29` passed.
- `test/gateway-queued-session-rotation.e2e.test.ts`: `2` passed.
- Materialized source hashes matched the local commit on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33715159753.
- Type-aware Oxlint passed on all touched files.
- Oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.

The focused tests also cover:

- a typed draining error while restart admission stays open;
- restart-signal rollback and queue resume;
- restart-signal promotion to one-way drain;
- synchronous retirement of queued turn ownership and stale callbacks.

Production LOC: `+33/-2` (net `+31`). The growth binds queue authority to the existing restart signal and closes the user-visible shutdown lifecycle gap. Tests: `+316/-0`.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted repair. The contributor's original restart-fence distinction and credit are preserved. Maintainer follow-up added the real Gateway reproduction, lifecycle retirement, and exact-head proof.

Claude Fable 5.1 binds each thinking block to the producing model and to the
exact request prefix that preceded it. Three harness behaviors conflicted with
that contract on Anthropic-family routes:

  while leaving Fable 5.1 still drops.
- The per-turn runtime-context carrier was injected transiently after the
  active user turn, stripped on the next request, relocated inside tool loops,
  and removed by the context-engine assembly. It is now persisted right after
  its user turn and replayed in place; inline inbound metadata stays in place
  too, and consecutive user turns are no longer merged at load for the
  Messages API because the merged form lost the second turn's timestamp stamp.
- Direct API-key requests with adaptive thinking send the
  thinking-binding-controls beta with prefix_mismatch_behavior=drop_block, so
  a residual mismatch degrades to a server-side unbilled drop with a warning
  listing the dropped paths instead of a 400, a duplicate request, and a
  transcript-wide thinking wipe. OAuth, proxies, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry
  keep the existing strip-and-retry recovery.

with tool loops and carriers reports input_transformations: [] on every
request with four retained thinking blocks; a /think change on the direct API
yields a logged server-side drop and no retry.

matched_commits.full_message:
fix(agents): preserve code blocks during duplicate collapse (#135945)

## What Problem This Solves

Every delivered assistant reply passes through `sanitizeUserFacingText`. Its final `collapseConsecutiveDuplicateBlocks` stage split the reply on blank lines without consulting code regions.

Repeated lines inside a fence could be deleted. Any duplicate elsewhere also caused retained fenced chunks to be trimmed, which removed meaningful indentation. The stored transcript stayed correct while channel users received corrupted code.

Fixes #135882

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared duplicate-paragraph projector keeps its incremental candidate detector. When that detector finds a possible duplicate, the canonical transform uses the existing parser-owned `findCodeRegions` ranges.

- Each code region becomes a deterministic unique token with no whitespace or line breaks.
- The existing prose collapse runs unchanged on the masked text.
- Unique tokens prevent code-touched paragraphs from comparing as duplicates and make code a sequence barrier.
- The exact parser-owned bytes replace the tokens after prose collapse.
- Streaming stays on the current fast path until a duplicate candidate appears.

This stays in the shared text-projection owner used by the sanitizer. It adds no Telegram branch and no second Markdown parser.

## User Impact

Telegram and other channel users receive fenced code with its indentation and repeated lines intact. Adjacent duplicate prose still collapses as before.

Production delta: +74/-6, net +68. Tests and test support: +139/-30, net +109. Current `main` absorbed the CI workflow, Chromium, and complete CLI-output repairs. The production growth carries the parser-owned block/inline distinction needed to preserve block code while retaining inline-prose duplicate collapse.

## Evidence

### Telegram Test Server

Ran the real Telegram direct-message path with the deterministic mock provider on baseline main `d413210bc7420923d101ce64211511cdac7b9464` and final exact head `8c740cc4e325c344108689738b266561285c5b0c` after integrating current main `fcbe9938d8c6b71917d4b70bdc8d2049d6c18547`.

The model response contained an indented Python method and three blank-line-separated repeated lines inside fenced code.

| Result | Current main | Exact head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delivered characters | 203 | 226, exact expected rendered text |
| `def log` indentation | column 0 | column 4 |
| `[worker] retrying` lines | 2 | 3 |
| Telegram code entities | 2 | 2 |
| Provider requests | 1 | 1 |
| Stored fenced transcript | exact | exact |

Exact delivered head text:

```text
Here is the retry loop and the log it produced:

class Worker:
    def run(self):
        self.log("retrying")

    def log(self, msg):
        print(msg)

[worker] retrying

[worker] retrying

[worker] retrying

[worker] done
```

The same run read the per-agent SQLite transcript before cleanup. It retained the original Markdown fences, indentation, and all three repeated lines.

### Tests and checks

- New regression test on current main: 3 expected failures for fenced bytes, initial indented code, and code-barrier reset.
- Current exact-head projection and sanitizer tests: 28 passed.
- Earlier full owner and sanitizer suites: 142 tests passed; delivery sibling suites: 228 tests passed.
- 12,960 generated code-free inputs matched the previous prose-collapse output.
- Oxfmt, Oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Prior Codex Sol autoreview: no accepted or actionable P0 findings. The exact-head landing review runs after push.
- CI root-cause repair: required comparison bases now load during the authenticated checkout. The guard, protocol, and npm-lock lanes no longer fetch after credentials are removed. Workflow and Git lifecycle suites passed 416 tests, and workflow validation passed.
- CI flake repair: the lease cleanup test now uses the existing 10-second worker-lifecycle lease, so constrained runners cannot turn its abort assertion into an unrelated lease-expiry result. The focused owner suite passed 10 tests.
- Windows CI cleanup repair: terminal test-instance cleanup now reuses the existing force-tree path on Windows, so inherited Gateway pipes cannot outlive completed assertions. The shared helper suite passed 36 tests; exact Windows proof runs in CI.
- Lease worker startup repair: the process-exit test now uses the existing compiled test-subprocess owner instead of launching a TypeScript child that can exhaust the production heartbeat readiness deadline. State lease suites passed 14 tests; compiled-subprocess inventory passed 39 tests.
- ClawSweeper review repairs: the original incremental duplicate projector now owns continuation suffixes after parser-backed reconciliation. A code-bearing regression keeps parser calls at one across 256 appends. The abort test now awaits heartbeat-worker exit before checking that lease state stays unchanged.
- Hosted Chromium repair: the corner-shape browser probe now treats the computed CSS alias `superellipse(1)` as semantic `round`. All 3 focused browser tests passed locally; exact hosted proof runs in CI.
- Built-CLI proof repair: finite CLI commands now wait for child stream closure and retain complete output, while long-lived Gateway logs remain bounded. The exact failed artifact emitted 288,423 bytes beyond the old 262,144-byte cap. The inherited-pipe and 300 KiB regressions pass with all 38 shared helper tests.

## ClawSweeper Rank-Up Moves

- Applied the remaining merge-risk move: parser-backed masking remains the single canonical code-protection path, while the existing suffix fast path and direct sanitizer and streaming regressions remain in place.
- Applied the inline-code move: parser-owned block regions remain unique barriers, while identical inline spans reuse stable tokens and collapse as ordinary prose across static and partitioned streaming input.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(gateway): distinguish socat forwards that name OpenClaw (#133381)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(gateway): distinguish socat forwards that name OpenClaw (#133381)

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway status` classified any listener whose process arguments contained `openclaw` as another Gateway.

A valid `socat` TCP forward can name OpenClaw in its arguments. For example, `-lpopenclaw` sets the forwarding process's logging name. When an OpenClaw Gateway and that forward listened on different addresses with the same numeric port, status kept the port busy but failed to identify `socat` as another process.

## Root Cause

Listener classification checked the full process arguments for `openclaw` before it checked the operating system's listener-owner command field.

The argument text is not executable identity. It can contain profile names, paths, logging labels, and forwarding targets.

## Fix

Check the inspected listener-owner command first. Treat `socat`, observed macOS `socat1`, and Windows `socat.exe` as non-Gateway owners before checking process arguments for OpenClaw.

This keeps an OpenClaw process launched with `--profile socat` classified as the Gateway. It also keeps the selected port busy while the forward is listening.

The repair removes the added command-line tokenizer and moves the regression to the `inspectPortUsage` owner boundary.

## User Impact

Gateway status now lists the real Gateway and the `socat` forward as different owners. Operators see the existing Gateway hint plus `Another process is listening on this port.`

## Evidence

Exact head: `bb27e573661c2685050f9f2448ea39fd6c6da06c`

- Current main `ae22204e7a20391ede4fb1ffb88d74709ff4af6f`, fresh secretless Linux container: a real profile named `socat` ran the Gateway on loopback. Real `socat -lpopenclaw` listened on the container address and forwarded to the same loopback port. Status reported the port busy and listed both listeners, but omitted the other-process hint.
- Exact head, same topology: status reported the port busy, listed both listeners, retained the Gateway hint, and added `Another process is listening on this port.`
- Anti-cheat: after stopping only `socat`, the profile-named Gateway remained busy and did not emit the other-process hint.
- Regression test: the new `inspectPortUsage` case failed against current-main production code for the missing other-process hint and passed on this head.
- Focused tests: the formatter, port-inspection, and real CLI process suites passed 126 tests with one platform skip.
- Process proof: the regression runs `gateway status --port ... --no-probe --json` through the shipped CLI entry process against a real Linux TCP listener whose operating-system command is `socat` and whose arguments name OpenClaw.
- Formatting: the four changed files passed `pnpm format:check`.
- Lint: the four changed files passed Oxlint with zero warnings and zero errors.
- Build: the production-identical predecessor `2904ce655c99eecc37386da92caa61d3802bdfd3` passed `pnpm build` in a fresh secretless container. Exact-head Blacksmith CI supplies the final build gate.

Production LOC: +8/-5, net +3. Tests: +133/-0. The production growth is the owner-command branch that prevents argument text from overriding listener identity.

matched_commits.full_message:
perf: Claude Code catalog refresh no longer re-scans the projects tree on every poll (#136222)

* perf(catalog): watch the Claude projects tree instead of re-statting it per poll

`sessions.catalog.list` took >1s in hundreds of requests per day (max 60s)
on an IOPS-saturated Gateway host. The Claude provider re-read the whole
`~/.claude/projects` tree on every poll to compute a freshness stamp
(readdir + stat of every direct child), and any active Claude session
changed that stamp so every poll also reran the assembled scan with a
realpath + stat per candidate; the Desktop 60s TTL forced CLI rescans too.
Measured warm poll on a 1.2k-project tree: ~7.2k stats, 1.2k readdirs,
1.5k realpaths with zero file parsing.

The provider now owns freshness with a directory watch
(`session-catalog-tree-watch.ts`): one recursive fs.watch on macOS and
Windows, root plus per-project-directory watches on Linux (Node's Linux
recursive watch watches every file), nonpersistent, degrading to a full
read on watcher failure with a 5s reattach. A watch vouches for coverage
only once it has been attached for 250ms and polled, because libuv starts
the FSEvents stream asynchronously and drops writes in that window. The
projects tree snapshot is kept per root and re-stats only dirty
directories; its lstat signatures (mtime/size/ino) replace the
per-candidate realpath + stat during discovery; CLI records are keyed by
tree stamp; the Desktop overlay refreshes on its own watch or backstop
without invalidating CLI records; Desktop custom groups cache on the
LevelDB listing signature; merged results are memoized on identity.

Gateway side, the list cache key no longer carries a per-connection
caller id. node.list and node.invoke read only scopes, role, and device
id from the caller and the key already carried those plus the profile
visibility facts, so a reconnected dashboard (a new client object) now
shares the settled enumeration instead of queueing another provider scan
behind the admission cap.

Warm unchanged poll after: 0 stats, 0 readdirs, 0 realpaths, 0 opens.

Docs: docs/providers/anthropic.md describes the watched freshness model.

matched_commits.full_message:
fix(imessage): sends keep failing with an opaque timeout after the private-API bridge dies (#134572)

The injected bridge helper can stop answering RPC while Messages.app stays alive
and the dylib stays mapped, so pgrep, channels status, and imsg status all keep
reporting it healthy. Sends then failed with a bare

  Internal error: code=-32603 Timed out waiting for response to 'send-message'

instead of the actionable "run imsg launch" guidance the unavailable path
already produces. In production this silently dropped a flight-arrival
notification.

- Annotate the stall at request(), the one choke point both capability-gated
  actions and normal sends funnel through, so the first failed send carries the
  cause and the repair. Normal delivery never consults the capability cache, so
  cache work alone could not reach it.
- Preserve the original error rather than replace it: send.ts reconciles delayed
  sends off data.disposition/data.retry_safe and matches
  /imsg rpc timeout \(send\)/i, so class, code, data, and the original message
  text all survive with guidance appended.
- Evict the never-expiring positive capability verdict on an observed stall, and
  key that eviction off the configured cliPath rather than the expanded one.
- Match only imsg's structured wait error. Local wrapper deadlines and ordinary
  rejections pass through untouched, each pinned by a test.

Eviction is a precondition, not a recovery: the re-probe still reads
imsg status --json, which is corrected separately in openclaw/imsg#253.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(ui): keep selected agent on native progress cards
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(ui): keep selected agent on native progress cards

Closes #135156

Supersedes #135223. The replacement keeps @rwinkelman's UI fix and removes the unrelated Gateway changes. Reported by @Synthetic2802.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using explicit multi-agent ownership could lose the selected agent when the Control UI loaded a native catalog session progress card. The Gateway then rejected the ownerless session key with `INVALID_REQUEST`, so the hovercard did not load.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog sidebar now uses the selected-agent-qualified session key for routed row actions such as `progressCard.get`. It keeps the ownerless catalog identity separately for source lookup and adoption matching.

The repair stays at the Control UI session-identity producer. It does not relax Gateway ownership checks or change configuration, storage, or protocol contracts.

## User Impact

Operators can select a non-default agent and open a native Codex catalog hovercard without an internal ownership error. The hovercard keeps its native title and workspace context.

## Evidence

- Exact-main red: `790bab7e300c03e1872fd4f644a9730a64957a32` sent `catalog:codex:...` from the real Control UI to a real isolated Gateway. Explicit ownership rejected it with `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- Exact-head green: `a68b895a3175172681b883ed94485cd661cf7659` sent `agent:writer:catalog:codex:...`; the real Gateway returned `progressCard.get` successfully.
- Anti-cheat probe: the route selected the non-default `writer` agent and the native catalog row came from the real Gateway catalog registry.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-catalogs.test.ts` — 330 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-progress-hovercard.e2e.test.ts` — 8 passed.
- Claude native-session E2E — 7 passed after its source-row selector moved to the preserved catalog identity attribute.
- Real Control UI/Gateway E2E — 1 passed on the exact head.
- Autoreview — clean, no accepted or actionable P0 findings.
- Production LOC: +10/-6, net +4. Tests and test support: +214/-4.

fix(memory-lancedb): preserve capture progress through compaction (#131329)

* fix(memory-lancedb): stop re-embedding old messages after cursor fingerprint eviction

resolveAutoCaptureStartIndex's fallback to a full rescan from index 0
(when the cursor's tracked message fingerprint can no longer be found,
e.g. after history compaction rewrites it) had no content-based guard
against reprocessing messages the cursor already captured earlier in
the same session. Once the fingerprint search missed once, every
subsequent turn re-embedded surviving old messages from the start of
history -- confirmed live as months-old conversation content being
re-submitted to the embedding endpoint continuously, at roughly 1
call/second for hours.

Track a bounded (20-entry) list of recently captured message
fingerprints on the cursor and skip already-captured messages by
content regardless of scan position, independent of
resolveAutoCaptureStartIndex's position-based resume heuristic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Vk2cBRQdErwRtPea8VuhG6

* fix(memory-lancedb): track duplicate-checked messages so they aren't re-embedded

The fingerprint guard added in the previous commit only marked a message
as captured when db.store() ran. When findCleanDuplicateMemory found an
existing match instead, the code skipped storing but never recorded the
fingerprint, so a message whose embedding had already been computed and
checked could still be re-embedded on a later fingerprint-miss rescan.

Track the fingerprint whenever the embedding-consuming work for a message
reaches a conclusion -- stored new or matched an existing duplicate --
since both are non-repeatable outcomes.

* test(memory-lancedb): prove survivor suppression against real OpenAI embeddings + LanceDB

ClawSweeper P1: the existing mocked-harness coverage for this fix
(index.test.ts's 're-embeds an already-captured surviving message once
its cursor fingerprint is evicted from history') spies on the embeddings
client and LanceDB runtime directly -- it proves this module's own
selection logic but not that a real configured plugin, real OpenAI
embeddings endpoint, and real LanceDB storage agree on the same call
count.

Added a live case to the existing memory-lancedb.live.test.ts (gated on
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 + OPENAI_API_KEY, already exercising real OpenAI
embeddings + real LanceDB for the store/recall/duplicate/forget flow) that
reproduces the exact compaction scenario: turn 1 captures two facts, turn
2 simulates a real compaction where the tracked message evicted from
history but an earlier, already-captured message survives verbatim ahead
of one genuinely new fact. OpenAIEmbeddingCallCounter counts real POST
requests to api.openai.com's /embeddings endpoint via a fetch wrapper
(same established pattern as the openai-responses continuation live
tests), so the assertion is on the real embedding provider's actual call
count, not a spy.

Confirmed this fails against the pre-fix production code (4 real
embedding calls -- the surviving message really did get re-embedded
against the live API) and passes with this branch's fix (3 calls).

Proof, real run against api.openai.com + real LanceDB:

$ OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENAI_API_KEY=*** node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-live.mts \
    extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.live.test.ts

 ✓ memory plugin live tests > memory tools work end-to-end 21828ms
 ✓ memory plugin live tests > does not re-embed a surviving auto-capture message after real compaction 561ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(ai): exclude tools from the HTTP continuation request-equality check (#132951)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(ai): exclude tools from the HTTP continuation request-equality check (#132951)

* fix(ai): exclude tools from the HTTP continuation request-equality check

`requestWithoutInput()` already excludes `instructions` from the
turn-to-turn request comparison in `resolveResponsesContinuationRequest`,
with the reasoning that it's rebuilt fresh every request from live
runtime state and comparing it just moves a false-positive rejection
into `request_changed`. `tools` was never given the same exclusion,
even though it's exactly the same class of field: the agent's
model-visible tool surface legitimately shifts turn to turn
(tool-search activation, session-scoped gating, MCP servers
connecting/disconnecting) independent of whether the prior turn's
server-side response state is still a valid continuation baseline.

Any ordinary tool-list change between two turns on the same connection
fell through to `request_changed`, silently and permanently disabling
HTTP continuation for the rest of that connection's life -- every
later attempt keeps comparing against the same now-stale cached tool
list. Confirmed live against a real OpenAI-Responses-compatible
endpoint: continuation held across a tool-calling round and a plain
new-turn round, then broke exactly at the turn where a second tool
became available, with `resolve: request_changed` and a JSON diff
whose only differing key was `tools`.

Add `tools` to the same destructure-and-drop as `instructions`, and a
regression test mirroring the existing `instructions` test that fails
pre-fix (`request_changed`) and passes post-fix (`continued`, with the
current turn's tools kept on the wire).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Vk2cBRQdErwRtPea8VuhG6

* fix(ai): trim invariant comment; prove tools-list-change continuation live against api.openai.com

Addresses ClawSweeper review on #132951:

- P2: HTTP continuation is native-api.openai.com-only on current main, so
  the earlier OmniRoute-only live proof didn't establish whether the
  official Responses API actually accepts previous_response_id after the
  turn's `tools` list changes, versus rejecting it. Added a live test
  (gated on OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 + OPENAI_API_KEY, matching the sibling
  continuation.live.test.ts pattern exactly, including the secret-recall
  proof that continuation genuinely resolved server-side history) that
  hits the real endpoint with a tool list that grows between turn 1 and
  turn 2. Passed: the real API accepts the changed tools with
  previous_response_id, the trimmed request never re-sent the secret, and
  the reply correctly recalled it -- proving genuine server-side
  continuation, not a lucky self-contained answer or a silent
  full-history fallback.
- P1: compressed the new `tools` exclusion comment to the short invariant
  (matching the sibling `instructions` comment's density) instead of
  restating the PR rationale, and pointed it at the new live test as the
  evidence backing the claim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Vk2cBRQdErwRtPea8VuhG6

* fix(ai): scope the tools-exclusion to HTTP continuation only

Addresses ClawSweeper P2 on #132951: resolveResponsesContinuationRequest
is shared by both the HTTP and WebSocket Responses transports. The
`tools` exclusion was only ever proven live over HTTP; WebSocket has its
own pre-existing test ("resets continuation on tool schema change" in
openai-responses-websocket.test.ts) asserting that a tool-schema change
resets continuation, which the unscoped exclusion silently broke for
that transport too, without any corresponding proof it's safe there.

Added a required `{ excludeTools: boolean }` option threaded through
`requestWithoutInput()`/`resolveResponsesContinuationRequest()` so every
caller states its own proof status instead of inheriting one implicitly:

- HTTP (`claimOpenAIResponsesHttpContinuation`): `excludeTools: true` --
  the option this PR's live evidence actually covers.
- WebSocket (`openai-responses-websocket.ts`): `excludeTools: false` --
  unchanged behavior, still resets on a tool-schema change, matching its
  existing test.
- Other call sites (compaction-replay test, cache-stability test): they
  don't vary tools, so `excludeTools: false` (the conservative default)
  doesn't change their outcome; passed explicitly since the parameter is

matched_commits.full_message:
fix(matrix): exclude code regions from spoiler collision predicate (#128453)

* fix(matrix): exclude code regions from spoiler collision predicate

`hasMatrixSpoilerMetadataCollision` flagged any `||` not already a
paired spoiler delimiter, escaped, or in a table. The delimiter finder
excludes code spans/blocks, so a `||` inside inline code or a fenced
block (e.g. `rg foo || true`) was not an ordinary delimiter and tripped
the collision — collapsing the whole message body to "[Spoiler]" and
losing all content, with no error or log on either side.

Exclude code regions in the collision predicate (matching the finder's
own exclusion) so a literal `||` in code is not mistaken for an
unresolvable spoiler attempt. Link metadata and tag attributes stay
fail-closed: a `||` there may be a spoiler the parser cannot safely
resolve, so it must still trigger the redaction.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(sessions): buildSessionContext never returns on a cyclic parent chain (#131567)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(sessions): buildSessionContext never returns on a cyclic parent chain (#131567)

buildSessionContext walks the parentId chain of whatever entry map it is
given, with no visited set. A map whose parentId links form a cycle drives
the walk until V8 refuses to grow the array -- 134,217,728 iterations, the
calling thread blocked throughout, ~2.5 GB allocated, then RangeError. The
input is not repo-controlled: the function is re-exported from
src/plugin-sdk/agent-core.ts and src/plugin-sdk/agent-sessions.ts.

Every other parent-chain walk under src/agents/sessions/ already guards
against this -- getBranch (session-manager-entries.ts:380), the branch walk
and its inner physical-parent walk (session-manager-branching.ts:41),
resolveCanonicalParentId (session-manager-core.ts:334), and the
opaque-to-canonical lookup (session-manager-core.ts:380) all carry a seen
set. This walk is the only one that does not.

Adopt the getBranch shape: track visited ids, stop on the first repeat and
return what was walked. Entry ids are unique within a map keyed by id, so an
acyclic chain can never repeat one and the guard never fires; behaviour
without a cycle is unchanged. Add a regression test that drives the exported
function directly with a two-node cycle.

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: fix(tool-display): don't render shell redirects or `rg --files` as search targets (#133783)
matched_commits.full_message:
fix(tool-display): don't render shell redirects or `rg --files` as search targets (#133783)

* fix(tool-display): don't render shell redirects or `rg --files` as search targets

`rg --files` takes no pattern, so every positional is a path, but the exec
summary read `positional[0]` as the pattern. `positionalArgs` also keeps shell
redirect tokens, and the summary uses the LAST positional as the target.

Together those made

    rg --files autonomy .openclaw 2>/dev/null

render as `search "autonomy" in 2>/dev/null`, naming a redirect as the path that
was searched. The same shape appeared in an agent failure notification, where it
read as though a file called `2>/dev/null` had been searched and sent debugging
down the wrong path.

Redirect filtering is deliberately applied only inside the grep/rg branch rather
than in `positionalArgs`. Other summaries already render redirect operators --
`cat > file <<EOF` renders as `show >` and is covered by an existing test -- so
filtering globally would change long-standing unrelated output.

fix(update): recover the managed gateway after a failed CLI update (#119516)

* fix(update): recover the managed gateway after a failed CLI update

A CLI-driven `openclaw update` stops the managed gateway before a mutable
update and recovers it through the guarded service adapter. Once the package
swap has completed, that updater process is older than the config the new
install wrote, so the future-config guard refuses its restart and the gateway
stays stopped behind a single warning line.

Gateway-initiated updates already avoid this: the detached handoff asks the
service manager to start the unit directly. Give the CLI path the same fallback
through the platform adapter, so launchd and Scheduled Tasks are covered too.
Ownership is still enforced; only the version guard is skipped, and only for
starting a unit this process stopped.

field, and the WCAG contrast reader follows the tint rule's :is(.user,

Copilot's ordinary steering branch dropped the sessions_send transcript
recorder: the SDK event bridge persisted its own user row without
provenance, so steered cross-session messages could not render as
forwarded bubbles. session.send now routes through the journal's

binding (safe when the event beats the send response), stamps the
recorder's provenance onto the SDK-built row, and satisfies the
recorder via runtime-persisted marks instead of a duplicate write.

The keyed directive pulled lit/directives/keyed into the boot graph for a
remount that cannot occur: messages are immutable and grouping splits on

protected behavior (titled chip survives re-renders). Startup JS returns
to 346,695 B, inside the committed baseline's growth allowance.

The titler, hovercard, and click handlers all reject keys without the

matched_commits.commit_message_snippet: perf(ui): stage the next history page so back-scroll prepends land instantly (#132737)
matched_commits.full_message:
perf(ui): stage the next history page so back-scroll prepends land instantly (#132737)

* perf(ui): stage the next history page so back-scroll prepends land instantly

After any consumed older page with more history remaining, the pane
fetches the next 400-message page in the background and parks it in a
single staging slot; the next boundary crossing applies it without a
round trip or the loading shimmer. The prefetch skips the last-writer-
wins request-ownership version (it could invalidate a concurrent tail
load) and instead carries a claim - client, epoch, session key, agent,
and the exact pagination cursor - validated at consume time; any drift
discards the page and the reactive path refetches. Viewport resets bump
a dedicated staging generation, reactive loads join an in-flight
prefetch instead of duplicating it, and prefetch failures stay silent
because the reactive path owns retries and blocked-until-intent.
Catalog sessions keep reactive loads: their opaque cursor pages apply
directly to pane state and cannot be parked.

Live proof on a seeded 1400-message session: gesture 1 shows the
loading boundary for 5 frames (cold fetch), gestures 2-4 prepend
100->500->900->1300->1400 with zero loading-state frames.

* fix(ci): register the channel-tool-progress attempt test in its codex lane

#132664 added run-attempt.channel-tool-progress.test.ts without adding it
to the enumerated app-server attempt lanes, so the vitest project
ownership guard fails on every full-suite run. Register it in the
attempt-extra lane.

* fix(ui): fence staged history pages against same-cursor projection resets

ClawSweeper P1: a rewind or branch switch resets the projection through
resetChatHistoryProjection, and the replacement branch can resume at the
identical pagination cursor - the staged page from the prior branch then
passed the claim check and would prepend stale rows. The claim now
captures historyVersion read-only at fetch time and the consume check
requires it unchanged, so every flow that takes history ownership (tail
reload, rewind, branch switch, reset) voids parked pages through the
existing owner. Regression stages a page, resets the projection, restores
the same cursor, and asserts the post-reset branch is refetched; it fails
without the fence.
